newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU drops dumping measures on Japan ball bearings.
newsitem.headline: EU drops dumping measures on Japan ball bearings.

text.p: The European Union said on Tuesday it had repealed anti-dumping measures imposed on small Japanese ball bearings and had ended an investigation into allegations of dumping.
It said in its Official Journal of April 29, published on Tuesday, that a review of interim measures imposed in September 1992 had concluded that the measures should be dropped.

The investigation into the imports of ball bearings of no more than 30 mm diameter was conducted on behalf of the French, Italian, Spanish and German units of Sweden's SKF, as well as FAG Kugelischer of Germany, Italy's FAG Cuscinetti and Umbra Cuscinetti, Portugal's Rolamentos Portugueses and France's SNR Roulements.
Japnese companies involved included Sapporro Precision, NTN Corporatoin, Nankai Seiko and NSK.

EU industry had claimed that "undercutting or lower price offers" by Japanese firms were imposing pressures on their own prices. The Japanese market share in the EU rose by 5.3 percent from 1991 to the investigation period.

But the investigation found in part that an increase in Japanese production reflected world-wide economic recovery and and a subsequent rise in demand for the industrial product. -- Brussels newsroom: +32 2 287-6830
